_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Drift Wood #11 · the Crab Derby
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; GULLY — aged 19, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Gully's uncle needs a flyer. Wood needs a subject. Everyone needs crab. Panel 1: a weathered shingle shack at a small-town boat launch in rain, a hand-painted crab derby sign, an older fisherman pointing at the wall, two teenage boys with a crab pot (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD). Uncle says "Gully says you draw. I need a flyer. Crab on it. Big.". Panel 2: a teenage boy in an overcoat with his hand on his chin, pained, at a boat launch (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "I was hoping to work in a more... Rohmer register. Quiet. Conversational. Crabless.". Panel 3: close-up of a weathered fisherman's flat face in a rain hood. Uncle says "Twenty bucks.". Wood says "Big crab.". Panel 4: a hand-drawn flyer taped to a wet shingle wall showing an enormous meticulously hatched crab, tiny text underneath, black and white. No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
